questions.q: What does a subnet mask tell a device?
options: Which port numbers are allowed through the firewall
Where the IP address splits between its network portion and its host portion
The MAC address of the default gateway
How fast the physical network link is
questions.explain: The subnet mask's 1-bits mark the network portion of the address and its 0-bits mark the host portion.

questions.q: What does /24 mean in CIDR notation?
options: 24 total addresses in the subnet
24 host bits
24 network bits, equivalent to a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0
The subnet uses port 24
questions.explain: The number after the slash is the count of network bits — /24 means 24 network bits, which is the same as the mask 255.255.255.0.

questions.q: In a /27 subnet, why are there only 30 usable host addresses out of 32 total?
options: Because /27 subnets are limited by law to 30 devices
Because the first address is reserved as the network address and the last is reserved as the broadcast address
Because 2 addresses are always reserved for DNS servers
Because half of all addresses in any subnet are reserved for future use
questions.explain: Every subnet reserves its first address as the network address (identifying the subnet) and its last as the broadcast address (reaching every host on it) — neither can be assigned to a device.

questions.q: What is the formula for how many usable host addresses a subnet has?
options: 2^(host bits)
2^(host bits) - 2
2^(network bits)
(host bits) x 2
questions.explain: Usable hosts = 2 raised to the number of host bits, minus 2 for the reserved network and broadcast addresses.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the practical reasons networks are broken into subnets?
options: Containing broadcast traffic within a smaller boundary
Isolating and securing groups of devices from each other
Making routing and troubleshooting easier by mapping a subnet to a physical location or logical group
Subnetting is required because IPv4 addresses would otherwise run out twice as fast
questions.explain: Subnetting doesn't change how many total addresses exist — it's about containment, isolation/security, and manageability, not address conservation.
